reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume (dimension zero is allowed), every V:E->R, every alpha,beta in the nonnegative reals, and every eta in R, assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C^2, eta>0, beta*eta<=1, and for all x,v in E, alpha*||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= beta*||v||^2. The Hessian is precisely the iterated Frechet derivative evaluated twice at v. There are no extra kernel, operator, invariance, spectral, or regularity inputs.

Set mu=vol_E.tilted(-V), namely normalized exponential tilting with weight exp(-V(x)). Let J be the pushforward of mu tensor gamma_E under (x,z)->(x,x+sqrt(eta) z), with gamma_E the standard Gaussian on E. Put nu=J.snd. Write H=L^2(nu;R) and K=L^2(J;R), spaces of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable square-integrable real functions, with their real Hilbert norms and inner products. Finite dimension of E does not make H or K finite-dimensional.

For every E,V,alpha,beta,eta satisfying the stated assumptions, use the measures mu,J,nu and Hilbert spaces H,K defined above. Define Lambda to be the pushforward of J under (x,y)->(y,2x-y), and define F(x,y)=(x,2x-y). Let P:K->K be conditional expectation in L^2(J) onto the sigma algebra generated by the second coordinate, followed by inclusion into K; equivalently P is the orthogonal projection onto the closed subspace of second-coordinate-measurable L^2 classes.

Then mu,J,nu are probability measures. There exists a Markov kernel S:E->E such that, for every y in E, S(y,dx) is exactly the normalized exponential tilt of canonical volume with exponent -V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta). Thus S(y,dx)=[exp(-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta))/Z_y] vol_E(dx), with Z_y the integral of this numerator. The formula holds for every state y, not merely almost everywhere. Lambda has S as a conditional kernel of its second coordinate given its first, so its disintegration is nu(dy) S(y,dx). Both marginals of Lambda equal nu.

There exists a real linear isometry U:K->K such that Ug=g composed with F, J-almost everywhere, for every g in K. U is involutive, meaning U(Ug)=g for every g, and its bounded continuous linear map is selfadjoint. There exists a real linear isometry M:H->K such that Mu(x,y)=u(y), J-almost everywhere, for every u in H. These maps and their properties are produced witnesses. In particular, M is an isometric embedding into K; the statement does not claim M maps onto all of K.

There exists a bounded continuous real linear operator T:H->H, selfadjoint, for which every u in H satisfies P(Mu)=Mu, M(Tu)=(P composed with U composed with P)(Mu), ||Tu||<=||u||, and Tu(y)=integral u(x) S(y,dx) for nu-almost every y. In addition, integral Tu dnu=integral u dnu for every u in H.

There exists q in H whose representative equals 1 nu-almost everywhere, with Tq=q. For every u in H, <q,u>=integral u dnu, and u belongs to ker(u-><q,u>) if and only if integral u dnu=0. This kernel H0 is the entire closed real subspace of H orthogonal to q, equivalently the entire mean-zero subspace, with the inherited Hilbert structure; it is not an arbitrary selected subspace.

On the entire space H define A=I_H-T composed with T. A is positive (its selfadjoint quadratic form is nonnegative), Aq=0, and <Au,u>=||u||^2-||Tu||^2 for every u in H. There exists a bounded continuous real linear endomorphism T0:H0->H0 whose value, included into H, equals Tu for every u in H0. T0 is selfadjoint and ||T0u||<=||u|| for every u in H0. With A0=I_H0-T0 composed with T0, A0 is positive, its value included into H equals Au for every u in H0, and <A0u,u>=||u||^2-||T0u||^2 for every u in H0. Thus both centered operators are actual restrictions of the corresponding full operators. All identities and positivity claims use the identity of their displayed full domain. No invertibility or quantitative strict contraction is asserted here.
